question:
During a classroom probability activity, a student first selects one of three boxes $B_1$, $B_2$ and $B_3$. The probabilities of selecting these boxes are $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{6}$ respectively. Box $B_1$ contains 4 red and 6 white counters, box $B_2$ contains 3 red and 2 white counters, and box $B_3$ contains 1 red and 4 white counters. After selecting a box, one counter is drawn at random from that box. Let $R$ denote the event that the counter drawn is red and $W$ denote the event that it is white.

(a) Verify that $B_1$, $B_2$ and $B_3$ form a valid partition for the selection process.

(b) Find $P(R|B_1)$, $P(R|B_2)$ and $P(R|B_3)$.

(c) Using the theorem of total probability, calculate $P(R)$.

(d) Determine $P(W)$ using the same partition and verify that $P(R)+P(W)=1$.
explanation:
(a)
The probabilities of selecting the three boxes are
$$P(B_1)=\frac{1}{2},\quad P(B_2)=\frac{1}{3},\quad P(B_3)=\frac{1}{6}$$
The selection of one box excludes the selection of either of the other two boxes, and one of the three boxes must be selected.
Also,
$$P(B_1)+P(B_2)+P(B_3)=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}=1$$
Hence, $B_1$, $B_2$ and $B_3$ form a valid partition for the selection process.

(b)
For box $B_1$,
$$P(R|B_1)=\frac{4}{10}=\frac{2}{5}$$
For box $B_2$,
$$P(R|B_2)=\frac{3}{5}$$
For box $B_3$,
$$P(R|B_3)=\frac{1}{5}$$
Thus, the required conditional probabilities are $\frac{2}{5}$, $\frac{3}{5}$ and $\frac{1}{5}$ respectively.

(c)
By the theorem of total probability,
$$P(R)=P(B_1)P(R|B_1)+P(B_2)P(R|B_2)+P(B_3)P(R|B_3)$$
Substituting the values,
$$P(R)=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{3}{5}+\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{1}{5}$$
$$P(R)=\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{30}=\frac{13}{30}$$
Hence, $P(R)=\frac{13}{30}$.

(d)
The probabilities of drawing a white counter are
$$P(W|B_1)=\frac{6}{10}=\frac{3}{5},\quad P(W|B_2)=\frac{2}{5},\quad P(W|B_3)=\frac{4}{5}$$
Therefore,
$$P(W)=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{3}{5}+\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{4}{5}$$
$$P(W)=\frac{3}{10}+\frac{2}{15}+\frac{2}{15}=\frac{17}{30}$$
Now,
$$P(R)+P(W)=\frac{13}{30}+\frac{17}{30}=1$$
Hence, the result is verified.

options.A:
(a) $B_1,B_2,B_3$ form a valid partition
(b) $P(R|B_1)=\frac{2}{5},\ P(R|B_2)=\frac{3}{5},\ P(R|B_3)=\frac{1}{5}$
(c) $P(R)=\frac{13}{30}$
(d) $P(W)=\frac{17}{30}$ and $P(R)+P(W)=1$
options.B:
(a) $B_1,B_2,B_3$ do not form a valid partition
(b) $P(R|B_1)=\frac{2}{5},\ P(R|B_2)=\frac{2}{5},\ P(R|B_3)=\frac{1}{5}$
(c) $P(R)=\frac{2}{5}$
(d) $P(W)=\frac{3}{5}$ and $P(R)+P(W)=1$
options.C:
(a) $B_1,B_2,B_3$ form a valid partition
(b) $P(R|B_1)=\frac{3}{5},\ P(R|B_2)=\frac{3}{5},\ P(R|B_3)=\frac{4}{5}$
(c) $P(R)=\frac{17}{30}$
(d) $P(W)=\frac{13}{30}$ and $P(R)+P(W)=1$
options.D:
(a) $B_1,B_2,B_3$ form a valid partition
(b) $P(R|B_1)=\frac{2}{5},\ P(R|B_2)=\frac{3}{5},\ P(R|B_3)=\frac{1}{5}$
(c) $P(R)=\frac{14}{30}$
(d) $P(W)=\frac{16}{30}$ and $P(R)+P(W)=1$
